AJAX|AJAX call: A way to send requests to the server from within an HTML page instead of the browser's address bar, e.g. when a button is pressed; "AJAX allows sending request to server" (slides 5, 6). See [XMLHttpRequest in four steps, readyState 0 to 4 and the status codes](#/comp4537-l5/xmlhttprequest-four-steps).
XMLHttpRequest|XHR: The browser object a page creates to send an AJAX request, "just like the way we created Date object": `let xhttp = new XMLHttpRequest();` (slide 7). See [XMLHttpRequest in four steps, readyState 0 to 4 and the status codes](#/comp4537-l5/xmlhttprequest-four-steps).
onreadystatechange: The property holding "the function that handles response"; it runs each time readyState changes (slide 8). See [XMLHttpRequest in four steps, readyState 0 to 4 and the status codes](#/comp4537-l5/xmlhttprequest-four-steps).
readyState: The "status of the XMLHttpRequest", 0 UNSENT, 1 OPENED, 2 HEADERS_RECEIVED, 3 LOADING, 4 DONE (slide 8; confirmed in Lecture 6 slide 55). See [XMLHttpRequest in four steps, readyState 0 to 4 and the status codes](#/comp4537-l5/xmlhttprequest-four-steps).
UNSENT: ReadyState 0, "The XHR object has been created, but open() has not been called yet" (slide 8). See [XMLHttpRequest in four steps, readyState 0 to 4 and the status codes](#/comp4537-l5/xmlhttprequest-four-steps).
OPENED: ReadyState 1, "open() has been called" (slide 8). See [XMLHttpRequest in four steps, readyState 0 to 4 and the status codes](#/comp4537-l5/xmlhttprequest-four-steps).
HEADERS_RECEIVED: ReadyState 2, "send() has been called, and the headers of the response are available" (slide 8). See [XMLHttpRequest in four steps, readyState 0 to 4 and the status codes](#/comp4537-l5/xmlhttprequest-four-steps).
LOADING: ReadyState 3, "The response is being received. As data comes in, the responseText property is updated"; can repeat when a large response arrives in chunks (slide 8). See [XMLHttpRequest in four steps, readyState 0 to 4 and the status codes](#/comp4537-l5/xmlhttprequest-four-steps).
DONE: ReadyState 4, "The operation is complete, and either the request has been successfully completed (status code 2xx) or an error occurred" (slide 8). See [XMLHttpRequest in four steps, readyState 0 to 4 and the status codes](#/comp4537-l5/xmlhttprequest-four-steps).
status|status code: The "http response type your server script returns": 200 OK, 3xx redirection, 4xx client error (403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found), 5xx server error (slide 8). See [XMLHttpRequest in four steps, readyState 0 to 4 and the status codes](#/comp4537-l5/xmlhttprequest-four-steps).
responseText: The response body as text, read in the handler once readyState is 4 and status is 200 (slide 8). See [XMLHttpRequest in four steps, readyState 0 to 4 and the status codes](#/comp4537-l5/xmlhttprequest-four-steps).
open()|xhttp.open: Step 3, `xhttp.open(method, url, Async or sync)`; method could be GET or POST, url is the file that handles the request (slide 9). See [XMLHttpRequest in four steps, readyState 0 to 4 and the status codes](#/comp4537-l5/xmlhttprequest-four-steps).
send()|xhttp.send: Step 4, sends the request; "we don't wait if we sent it asynchronously"; its optional argument is the request body, ignored for GET or HEAD (slides 9, 27). See [XMLHttpRequest in four steps, readyState 0 to 4 and the status codes](#/comp4537-l5/xmlhttprequest-four-steps).
async|asynchronous request: `true` as open()'s third argument; the script carries on without waiting for the response (slide 9). See [XMLHttpRequest in four steps, readyState 0 to 4 and the status codes](#/comp4537-l5/xmlhttprequest-four-steps).
query string: The `?name=John` part of a GET URL carrying the arguments; several are joined with `&` ("John&age=23") (slide 14). See [Demo 1 and Demo 2: a GET with and without a query string](#/comp4537-l5/ajax-get-demos).
CORS|Cross-Origin Resource Sharing: "a security feature implemented in web browsers and is configured by the contacted server in the response's header to the AJAX requests made via the browser" (slide 18). See [CORS, the Same-Origin Policy and the preflight request](#/comp4537-l5/cors-and-the-same-origin-policy).
Same-Origin Policy|SOP: The browser's default policy: "the html files containing the AJAX requests have to be hosted in the same origin that also hosts the server side scripts" (slide 18). See [CORS, the Same-Origin Policy and the preflight request](#/comp4537-l5/cors-and-the-same-origin-policy).
origin: "defined by the combination of domain, protocols and ports ( 80 is the default for HTTP, 443 for HTTPS)" (slide 18, footnote 3). See [CORS, the Same-Origin Policy and the preflight request](#/comp4537-l5/cors-and-the-same-origin-policy).
cross-origin request: "When a web page hosted in originA needs to cross and send requests to a server in another origin, originB"; browsers block it unless the server explicitly allows it (slide 18). See [CORS, the Same-Origin Policy and the preflight request](#/comp4537-l5/cors-and-the-same-origin-policy).
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: The response header that "tells the browser what origins can send requests to this server"; `"*"` means all origins (slide 19). See [CORS, the Same-Origin Policy and the preflight request](#/comp4537-l5/cors-and-the-same-origin-policy).
Access-Control-Allow-Methods: Response header listing the HTTP methods the server allows for cross-origin requests (slide 20 asks; answer worked out in the lesson). See [CORS, the Same-Origin Policy and the preflight request](#/comp4537-l5/cors-and-the-same-origin-policy).
Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Response header listing the request headers, such as Content-Type, the server allows (slide 20 asks; answer worked out in the lesson). See [CORS, the Same-Origin Policy and the preflight request](#/comp4537-l5/cors-and-the-same-origin-policy).
preflight request|preflight: An OPTIONS request the browser sends first to check whether the server permits the intended cross-origin request, e.g. a POST with Content-Type application/json (slides 20, 29 ask; answer worked out in the lesson). See [CORS, the Same-Origin Policy and the preflight request](#/comp4537-l5/cors-and-the-same-origin-policy).
OPTIONS: The HTTP method of the preflight request; the server answers it with the Access-Control-Allow headers and no body (slide 20 asks; answer worked out in the lesson). See [CORS, the Same-Origin Policy and the preflight request](#/comp4537-l5/cors-and-the-same-origin-policy).
Postman: A non-browser client for sending API requests; CORS does not apply to it because CORS is implemented in web browsers (slide 21 asks; slide 18). See [CORS, the Same-Origin Policy and the preflight request](#/comp4537-l5/cors-and-the-same-origin-policy).
header|request header: "a piece of information about the data sent via HTTP request"; it tells the server what type of data is enclosed, its formatting and language; a request can carry several, each a name and value pair (slide 27). See [POST with AJAX: the body, the Content-type header and data in chunks](#/comp4537-l5/post-with-ajax).
application/x-www-form-urlencoded: The content type that "describes form data that is sent in a single block in the HTTP message body" (slide 27). See [POST with AJAX: the body, the Content-type header and data in chunks](#/comp4537-l5/post-with-ajax).
setRequestHeader: The XHR method that adds a request header, e.g. `setRequestHeader("Content-type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")` (slide 27). See [POST with AJAX: the body, the Content-type header and data in chunks](#/comp4537-l5/post-with-ajax).
request body: Where POST puts its data: "For POST, the query string sits in the body of the request" (slides 23, 27). See [POST with AJAX: the body, the Content-type header and data in chunks](#/comp4537-l5/post-with-ajax).
chunk|data chunk: A piece of the POST body; `req.on('data')` "gets called when something has been read from the stream" and data may come in multiple chunks (slides 24, 28). See [POST with AJAX: the body, the Content-type header and data in chunks](#/comp4537-l5/post-with-ajax).
end event|req.on('end'): "gets called when stream has ended ( all data from cleint has arrived to server)"; the server parses the collected body here (slide 28). See [POST with AJAX: the body, the Content-type header and data in chunks](#/comp4537-l5/post-with-ajax).
CRUD: Create a table or DB, Read from a DB, Update records on a DB, Delete a record or Drop a table (slide 32). See [Connecting Node to MySQL: createConnection, connect, query](#/comp4537-l5/node-to-mysql).
MySQL|MariaDB: The relational DB engine that runs the SQL statements; XAMPP installs it as MariaDB (MySQL), on port 3306 (slides 32, 34, 36). See [Connecting Node to MySQL: createConnection, connect, query](#/comp4537-l5/node-to-mysql).
XAMPP: "an application package installer" that installs the DB engine (MySQL) and the DB admin tool (phpMyAdmin) (slides 34, 35). See [Connecting Node to MySQL: createConnection, connect, query](#/comp4537-l5/node-to-mysql).
phpMyAdmin: "a web based database administrative tool"; it needs the PHP engine to run (slide 35). See [Connecting Node to MySQL: createConnection, connect, query](#/comp4537-l5/node-to-mysql).
npm install mysql: Installs `mysql`, "an external module" Node does not ship; without it Node stops with "Cannot find module 'mysql'" (slide 43). See [Connecting Node to MySQL: createConnection, connect, query](#/comp4537-l5/node-to-mysql).
createConnection|mysql.createConnection: Step 1, "create a mysql object" from host, user, password and database (slide 44). See [Connecting Node to MySQL: createConnection, connect, query](#/comp4537-l5/node-to-mysql).
connect|con.connect: Step 2, "Then connect"; its callback gets `err` and logs "Connected!" when there is none (slide 44). See [Connecting Node to MySQL: createConnection, connect, query](#/comp4537-l5/node-to-mysql).
query|con.query: Step 3, "run a SQL statement": `con.query(sql, function (err, result) {…})` (slide 44). See [Connecting Node to MySQL: createConnection, connect, query](#/comp4537-l5/node-to-mysql).
AUTO_INCREMENT: Column option that numbers new rows automatically; scoreID in the score table, which skipped from 1 to 3 (slides 39, 45). See [Connecting Node to MySQL: createConnection, connect, query](#/comp4537-l5/node-to-mysql).
